data.title: Amazon Business targets procurement efficiency with new AI and reporting features
data.description:
Almost one year after Amazon Business unveiled its Amazon Business Assistant in 2025, the business-to-business (B2B)-focused side of Amazon announced two ways in which it will seek to improve procurement for the buyers that it serves.

The new capabilities, revealed at the Amazon Business Reshape event in Nashville on Oct. 27, cover new Business Assistant enhancements, as well as an experience that the company refers to as Amazon Business Value Intelligence.

Both announcements include visibility and options aimed at procurement pain points in hopes of boosting Amazon Business sales.

What Amazon Business is adding to its procurement experience

Amazon characterized the new Business Assistant abilities as an expansion “from a general-purpose resource into a conversational tool that speaks to each customer’s business account orders, spend, and activity” in a blog post published Oct. 27.

“Every hour a procurement team spends chasing approvals or manually reconciling invoices is an hour they’re not spending on the work that moves their organization forward,” said Shelley Salomon, worldwide vice president of Amazon Business, in a released statement. “Amazon Business Assistant now steps in to handle the repetitive, time-consuming tasks that slow teams down, so they can focus on finding the right products, managing supplier relationships, and driving real value across their business.”

Specifically, the Business Assistant enhancements included order tracking, approvals process information, savings recommendations, integrated payment allocation options and spending analysis.

The features are available to Amazon Business customers in the U.S. through their account pages.

What is Amazon Business Value Intelligence?

Meanwhile, Amazon Business Value Intelligence will offer U.S.-based buyers new ways to understand savings, operational efficiency and purchase compliance. The information will be based on an organization’s own Amazon Business data, viewed alongside third-party benchmarks that Amazon Business tracks.

“Procurement has always been about more than price, but price is what gets reported because it’s the easiest thing to measure,” said Salomon. “We designed Value Intelligence to change the conversation from ‘what did this cost?’ to ‘what value is procurement creating?'”

Amazon Business is positioning Value Intelligence as a tool to communicate these outcomes to management and finance teams.

“Now leaders can see the savings, time back, and off-policy spend prevented in one view, and confidently show the full impact of their buying strategy, not just the price,” she stated.

The company pitched the features as means to lend credibility to strategy and decisions with data to support its conclusions. Ultimately, the intent is to provide procurement managers with reports that can be shared in their organizations so that finance teams can reconcile numbers and parties can align on stories about results and value being produced.

data.title: Walmart unveils AI agent shopping controls, spending limits
data.description:
Walmart wants its shoppers to stay in control as artificial intelligence (AI) agents take on a bigger role across ecommerce.

The retailer is rolling out new tools designed to let customers oversee AI agent purchases, streamline how agents shop and set boundaries for what they can and cannot do on shoppers’ behalf.

Announced Wednesday (Oct. 21), the changes are designed to support agentic commerce across Walmart and Sam’s Club. Walmart acknowledged that not everyone will want to shop using AI agents. But for those who do, the retailer said its goal is to “make our experience the most trusted” by building safeguards into the shopping process.

To support that, Walmart is introducing three updates:

  • Agent Profiles: To let shoppers authorize AI agents, set spending limits and track purchases.
  • Agent Gateway: For giving agents a more direct connection to Walmart’s shopping services.
  • New purchasing rules: Setting limits on agents’ actions and access to customer information.

Beyond changes for shoppers, Walmart is helping its marketplace sellers prepare for AI-driven product discovery, which could open up new opportunities to reach customers.

The move builds on Walmart’s existing AI shopping efforts. These include its Sparky AI shopping agent and integrations with Meta’s Muse, OpenAI ChatGPT and Google’s Gemini. The retailer has not specified which agents will support the new profiles at launch.

Walmart ranks No. 2 in Digital Commerce 360’s Top 1000 Database. The market research tool tracks North America’s largest online retailers by their annual ecommerce sales.

Walmart is No. 37 in Digital Commerce 360 and ReFiBuy’s AI Commerce Rankings. That set of rankings is available in the Top 1000 Pro with AI Database.

How Walmart’s AI agent profiles will work

Walmart said it plans to launch Agent Profiles within the next month, giving shoppers a way to oversee AI-led purchases.

Currently, purchases made by AI agents appear alongside customers’ own orders in their Walmart accounts, with no way to tell them apart. The new feature will allow agents to “shop using dedicated profiles linked to a customer’s account, so customers can approve purchases, set spending limits, and see which purchases were made by an agent,” Daniel Danker, Walmart’s executive vice president of AI acceleration, product and design, said in a LinkedIn post.

Through Agent Profiles, shoppers can choose to approve AI purchases one at a time. Alternatively, they can allow agents to spend up to a preset limit, such as $50, $100 or $200.

The company outlined three steps for setting up an Agent Profile:

  • Start in the agent’s app: Walmart creates a profile when a customer first shops through its Agent Gateway.
  • Connect to Walmart: Customers sign in to their Walmart accounts to authorize and link the agent’s profile.
  • Set spending controls: Shoppers choose a spending limit, review purchases made by agents and can delete profiles at any time.

On Walmart’s website, agents will see “the same prices that a human would see,” with offers and fees displayed before purchase, the company noted.

What protections apply when AI agents shop?

Walmart is also “setting expectations for how AI agents work with customers and our company,” Danker said.

These safeguards come as consumers remain wary of giving AI control over purchases. In survey results published in August, payments technology provider NMI asked 1,000 U.S. adults about AI shopping. Only 11% of those surveyed reported using AI to complete a transaction. Meanwhile, 70% wanted the ability to review or override an AI purchasing decision before checkout. Only 10% said they would give AI full control over a purchase.

Addressing concerns, Walmart said its new terms require customers to approve agent purchases by default. Shoppers can authorize spending within preset limits, though the company said it could still require additional approval.

The rules also bar agents from acting beyond a shopper’s instructions, accessing unauthorized information or receiving payment-card details, according to Walmart. Additionally, agents cannot add or change payment methods.

If an agent makes an unintended purchase, Walmart said its existing returns process will apply. Agents that violate the terms will be blocked from its website.

Even so, information shoppers share directly with third-party AI apps remains subject to those providers’ privacy policies, the company said.

Walmart builds a direct connection for AI agents

Walmart is also developing the Agent Gateway, which gives AI systems a faster, more direct way to shop with the retailer.

Currently, agents use a browser to shop following steps designed for people. “This can be slow and error-prone, and agents may get stuck along the way,” Walmart said.

The Agent Gateway aims to address this using Model Context Protocol (MCP). The open standard developed by Anthropic allows AI applications to connect with external tools and services.

The gateway supports “discovery, add to cart, purchasing, and order tracking,” Danker said. It is also designed to help agents find products customers regularly buy without giving them access to sensitive customer information.

For example, Walmart said it could help an agent find a customer’s preferred brand of milk or bread “without sharing the customer’s broader shopping history.”

The gateway will launch in limited beta for companies and developers, though Walmart has not announced when or who will participate.

How agentic shopping could benefit Walmart Marketplace sellers

Agentic commerce is already changing how some Walmart shoppers find products, opening up new opportunities for marketplace sellers.

Speaking at Morgan Stanley’s Technology, Media and Telecom Conference in March, Danker said vitamin and protein supplements were the top two product types purchased from Walmart through ChatGPT. He suggested those purchases may have begun as broader conversations rather than searches for specific products.

That shift is a “potential game-changer” for sellers, said Manish Joneja, senior vice president of Walmart Global Marketplace and Walmart Fulfillment Services.

In a statement shared with Digital Commerce 360, Joneja said agentic commerce “could create more opportunities for sellers to put the right products in front of the right customers, including brands and products that may not have broad awareness.”

But it could also raise the bar for sellers. Joneja said accurate product information, competitive prices, availability and reliable delivery promises will all become increasingly important.

To prepare, Walmart is working with marketplace sellers to improve listings and catalog quality, he said. The changes will help make their products “easier for AI-powered shopping experiences to understand and recommend.”

data.title: Salesforce to acquire Braze for $5.66 billion to expand AI-powered marketing
data.description:
Salesforce plans to acquire Braze for $5.66 billion, making an artificial intelligence (AI) play for technology to help brands respond to shopper behavior in real time.

Under the definitive agreement announced Oct. 20, Braze shareholders would receive $47.50 per share in cash. That represents a roughly 58% premium over the stock’s Oct. 19 closing price.

Salesforce expects the acquisition to strengthen its Marketing Cloud business and broader AI offerings.

“Braze was built to turn live customer behavior into personalized engagement at scale,” said Patrick Stokes, president of applications and marketing at Salesforce, in the acquisition announcement. “Bringing that capability together with Salesforce Marketing Cloud, CRM and Data 360 will deliver that wow moment in every customer interaction.”

The transaction is expected to close during Salesforce’s fiscal 2028, which runs from Feb. 1, 2027, through Jan. 31, 2028. The deal remains subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals. Salesforce said it does not expect the acquisition to affect its fiscal 2027 financial guidance.

In North America, 78 of the Top 2000 online retailers use Salesforce as their ecommerce platform, according to Digital Commerce 360 data. Together, those retailers generated more than $192.60 billion in web sales in 2025. The Top 2000 is Digital Commerce 360’s database ranking North America’s largest online retailers by annual ecommerce sales.

What Salesforce gains from Braze’s AI capabilities

New York-based Braze specializes in personalized marketing across mobile apps, websites, email and other digital channels. Using real-time customer data and AI, its platform helps brands optimize the message, timing and channel for customer interactions.

Braze would bring considerable scale to Salesforce’s marketing business. Its platform serves roughly 2,770 customers, including Urban Outfitters, Instacart and Canva. Urban Outfitters is No. 29 in the Top 2000.

In a LinkedIn post on Oct. 20, Braze co-founder and chief technology officer Jon Hyman shared that the platform engages 9 billion monthly active users across its customer base. In 2025, Braze also handled “about 4.5 trillion messages and other actions to consumers,” he wrote.

A key part of the deal is BrazeAI, which combines predictive, generative and agentic AI. According to Braze, the tools can anticipate customer behavior, generate marketing content and optimize when, where and how brands reach shoppers.

How Salesforce plans to integrate Braze

For Salesforce, Braze could fill a gap in its existing marketing business.

The acquisition would give Salesforce “a real-time engagement layer that its marketing business has historically lacked,” Shay Boloor, chief market strategist at Futurum Equities, told Reuters.

Salesforce plans to connect Braze’s real-time marketing technology with Customer 360, its suite of customer data and applications spanning sales, marketing, commerce and service. The ecommerce platform and software provider expects the combination to strengthen Marketing Cloud, which businesses use to manage marketing campaigns.

With access to Salesforce’s customer data, Braze’s technology could help marketers “adapt engagement as customers browse, buy, and use products,” according to the acquisition announcement.

Salesforce also expects Braze’s AI capabilities to work alongside Agentforce, its platform for deploying AI agents that can make decisions and carry out tasks. The combination could help businesses better coordinate marketing with ecommerce, sales and customer service, Salesforce said.

Meanwhile, Braze CEO and co-founder Bill Magnuson said Salesforce’s technology, reach and partner network would help the company “bring more of our vision to market sooner.”

In an Oct. 20 LinkedIn post, Magnuson also said he would remain CEO and that the company would continue operating as Braze.

How retailers are using Braze to drive sales

Some retailers are already reporting higher engagement and conversion rates from campaigns using Braze’s technology.

Grove Collaborative, a sustainability-focused online retailer, switched to Braze after its previous marketing platform couldn’t support real-time personalization. The system had also crashed on Thanksgiving Eve, according to a Braze case study.

Integrating Braze with its Shopify storefront allowed Grove to automate personalized reminders and product suggestions for shoppers who browsed without buying. The resulting campaign generated a 10% checkout rate, a 41% add-to-cart rate and a 3% click-through rate, according to Braze.

E.l.f. Beauty Inc. offers another example. The beauty retailer partnered with Braze and Stitch to expand its mobile marketing efforts and boost engagement with its loyalty program, Beauty Squad.

With help from the two companies, e.l.f. expanded its use of push notifications and personalized in-app campaigns to encourage customers to return to its mobile app. Between March and September 2023, monthly mobile app usage increased 125%, according to a separate Braze case study.

The retailer also added push notifications to its existing loyalty emails, reminding Beauty Squad members to redeem rewards before they expired. Those efforts, alongside other support from Braze, contributed to a 58% year-over-year increase in loyalty offer redemptions in 2024, according to the study.

Grove ranks No. 256 in the Top 2000, while e.l.f. Beauty ranks No. 328.

Salesforce expands AI capabilities through acquisitions

The Braze deal is part of Salesforce’s push to expand its AI offerings through in-house development and acquisitions.

That strategy comes as Salesforce’s existing AI business gains traction. In its fiscal second quarter, Agentforce annual recurring revenue surpassed $1.5 billion, up 240% year over year. Combined with Data 360, annual recurring revenue reached $3.9 billion, according to the company’s earnings results.

Meanwhile, the company has made several other sizable acquisitions this year. In September, it completed its $3.6 billion deal to acquire Fin, which develops AI agents for handling customer service inquiries.

That same month, it acquired Contentful for roughly $1.5 billion to support more personalized customer experiences.

More recently, Salesforce announced an agreement to acquire Listen Labs, which uses AI agents to conduct customer research and analyze feedback. Financial terms were not disclosed.

data.title: Etsy updates AI policy, noting concerns about buyer trust
data.description:
Etsy published updated guidelines on artificial intelligence (AI) for sellers on Oct. 22. The marketplace is restricting specific categories of AI-generated content, tightening listing photo requirements and introducing new enforcement tools.

The changes signal a larger effort to protect buyer trust, which Etsy says is being eroded as AI-generated listings proliferate across the platform.

“AI should support your creativity and craftsmanship, not replace them,” Etsy vice president of customer operations James Ossman wrote in the update. “Buyers should always be able to understand the role you play in every item you sell on Etsy.”

Etsy is No. 20 in Digital Commerce360’s Global Online Marketplaces Database. The market research tool ranks the 100 largest marketplaces by third-party gross merchandise value (GMV).

How Etsy’s new AI guidelines work

Etsy’s seller handbook now includes a categorical ban on AI-generated functional guides, including patterns, recipes or instructions. Listings for these items must also show a real result made using the seller’s own instructions, not an AI-generated image of what the finished product might look like.

In addition, Etsy now requires that every listing include at least one unedited photo of the actual item against a real background. Supplemental images can still use AI-assisted editing to adjust lighting, color, cropping or backgrounds, but all photos must accurately represent the item a buyer will receive.

Notably, the marketplace is not banning AI-generated art outright. The policy continues to allow it when sellers play a clear creative role in its creation, such as a fantasy illustration based on the seller’s own prompt and creative direction. Sellers must still disclose when an item is created using AI and cannot misrepresent AI-generated work as handmade.

Bot-generated listings without human involvement are explicitly prohibited and will result in listing removal, Etsy said.

How Etsy will enforce the new rules

Meanwhile, Etsy says it will alert sellers if it detects AI-generated images during the listing process. It intends to provide guidance to help sellers meet requirements.

Looking ahead, the marketplace said it will expand that detection to existing listings over time. Sellers whose listings are removed can appeal through the Policy violations page in Etsy’s Shop Manager options.

Etsy is also adding a new buyer-facing reporting option so consumers can flag listings that they believe are AI-generated. Those reports will initially inform Etsy’s understanding of how buyers perceive AI misuse, rather than trigger immediate enforcement action, with removal activity expanding in the coming months as detection tools improve.

Etsy’s evolving relationship with AI

As it tightens AI restrictions on sellers, Etsy also continues to use AI itself. 

As Digital Commerce 360 reported in August, CEO Kruti Goyal described Etsy’s AI strategy as focused on three areas: improving product discovery, delivering more personalized shopping experiences, and experimenting with agentic and conversational commerce. 

“We see the biggest opportunity for AI on Etsy itself,” Goyal said on the company’s Q2 earnings call. “It’s really about using AI to make Etsy much, much better at connecting the right buyers with the right sellers.”

Etsy has partnered with OpenAI, Google and Microsoft on agentic commerce,  announced it would sell directly through Google AI Mode in January and is a backer of Google’s Agent Payments Protocol. Goyal said in August that agentic AI experiences still account for less than 1% of Etsy’s traffic, though the referrals that do come through AI channels carry higher buyer intent and average order value than typical traffic.

In 2025, Etsy rolled out AI-powered tools for sellers, including a writing assistant that mimics a seller’s voice, bulk listing suggestions and AI-generated review highlights.

data.title: Staples Canada launches Staples Business to unify B2B offerings
data.description:
Staples Canada has launched Staples Business, a new brand in the market to bring office supplies, technology, print and facilities services together for Canadian business customers.

The brand will focus on two tiers: one for smaller businesses and one for larger buyers that need custom pricing and dedicated account support.

Richmond Hill, Ontario-based Staples Canada said the new brand would simplify purchasing and account management for business customers.

Why Staples Business is launching in Canada

“Staples Business brings everything our business customers rely on together under one brand, building on our long-standing commitment to supporting Canadian businesses for more than 30 years,” said Chris Saniga, chief B2B officer at Staples Canada. “As a Canadian company, we understand the pressures organizations here are facing. Whether it’s a growing startup or a large enterprise, our goal is to take more off their plate so they can focus on what comes next.”

Currently, Staples has nearly 300 outlets in Canada. Its Quebec stores operate under the Bureau en Gros nameplate.

Industry analysts assessed that the new brand’s debut is as much about competition as customer service.

Marty Bauer, ecommerce expert at Omnisend, an email and SMS marketing platform for ecommerce brands, said the move was necessary to fend off competition.

“This new branding strategy is about much more than a cosmetic rebrand,” Bauer stated. “It’s an important step in defending the market against ecommerce giants, particularly Amazon Business.”

What makes Staples Canada’s business customer unique?

Bauer noted that B2B clients are quite different from regular shoppers in Staples Canada’s case.

“The goal is to make supply procurement as easy and frictionless as possible,” he said. “It’s as much about time and efficiency as it is about price. The new, refreshed Staples Business aims to offer exactly that.”

Bauer added that Staples Business has brought together a wide range of products, from office and janitorial supplies to IT hardware.

“This means a single account manager is responsible for all of a client’s needs, which significantly lowers administrative hassle for both parties,” Bauer said.

Additionally, Bauer pointed out that Staples Business will be able to categorize its clients into different tiers. Different-sized businesses require different approaches. For instance, small-to-medium businesses (SMBs) may place greater emphasis on an automated checkout system, transparency and fast response times than larger companies. Meanwhile, large businesses, Bauer explained, expect dynamic contract pricing, custom product catalogs and dedicated account managers.

“Staples Business is now better able to cater to these different needs,” Bauer said.

How Staples Business will try to compete in Canada

Lastly, Bauer said, a dedicated B2B brand could show Staples Canada’s business customers that a company is serious about catering to them and can compete with ecommerce giants.

“They may not be able to compete in terms of pricing, but they can compete in terms of expertise and the ability to cater to clients’ specific needs,” Bauer said.

Another observer said the brand’s success will depend on whether Staples can deliver on its promise.

Rich Pleeth, founder of the artificial intelligence (AI)-powered logistics platform Finmile, said a dedicated business brand can help Staples Canada win customers by making its wider offer easier to understand.

“Someone who thinks of Staples for printer paper may not think of it for IT support or facilities supplies,” Pleeth stated. “Putting those services together gives the sales team a clearer story, but the customer still needs a reason to change suppliers.”

Pleeth echoed Bauer’s perspective, adding that a small business might be persuaded by the prospect of less time spent ordering and chasing deliveries.

“For a larger buyer, consolidated invoicing, agreed pricing and an account manager who can sort out a problem could be worth more than a small discount on stationery,” Pleeth said. “The two tiers make sense because those buyers need different levels of support.”

Nevertheless, Pleeth expects that the new name will present a test.

“If a business orders laptops, chairs and printed materials for a new office, can someone coordinate the delivery and resolve anything missing?” he asked. “If the customer still has to chase three departments, the brand has promised more than the operation delivers.”
